entries.note: The CLI extracts legacy sealed-room blobs. It does not open a workspace folder.
The legacy content getters and updater read or write blob bytes only after rejecting workspace databases.
Legacy inserts and byte-deduplication use this column only after the shared workspace-database guard refuses workspace storage.
The shared fail-closed guard documents that files.original_bytes belongs only to legacy blob rooms.
Legacy search and byte inventory queries read the blob column; workspace callers route through WorkspaceService instead.
The hybrid recording path documents and enforces that recovered workspace WAV bytes stay out of the legacy blob column.
The nullable column remains for old rooms. Workspace rows must keep it NULL.
Legacy blob version snapshots read this column. WorkspaceService uses encrypted content objects instead.
The hybrid transcript edit path documents that workspace snapshots must not copy current audio into the legacy blob column.
Conversion streams source blobs, verifies them, and clears the column only in the new workspace copy.
Conversion planning checks whether each legacy source blob exists before scheduling a workspace copy; it never reads workspace current bytes from this column.
The reference documents the invariant; workspace reads and writes are routed to WorkspaceService.
Sealed import projects current files into normal files and explicitly stores NULL in workspace rows.
This aggregate reports bytes still owned by the legacy blob store.
Legacy repair streams old blob bytes into a normal file and then clears the column as it adopts the row into workspace storage.
Workspace file creation and object publication insert NULL; current bytes are written only to normal files.
Filesystem reconciliation registers normal files with NULL legacy bytes and never copies their current content into the database.
